central_claim: Across 38 modelled in-frame NR4A3 fusion junctions, 190 junction-spanning 5-6-5 gapmers were tiled and put through five in-silico specificity screens, and nearly half (87 of 190, 45.8%) let a mature wild-type parent transcript pair the whole catalytic gap over at least ten contiguous base pairs — a liability that is a property of joining two exon termini rather than of this disease, since exon-terminus chimeras meet the same screen at 40.6%, inside the panel's own 95% interval. Selecting within each junction rather than across the panel nevertheless yields two nameable reagents at the two most-reported breakpoints (EWSR1 e12 and TAF15 e6, both to NR4A3 exon 3), whose longest wild-type parent gap duplexes are 8 and 9 bp against wild-type TFG, together with two screened scramble controls and a pre-registrable selectivity threshold and power calculation. Nothing was synthesised or tested; every count is a prediction from sequence search, no efficacy, potency or safety is claimed, and the paper states that the two published fusion-positive EMC cell models are reported at an NR4A3 exon-2 acceptor rather than this panel's.
